title: Lazy KV handoff and degrade schedule for OOM reduction
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Reduce GPU OOM incidents during high concurrency by introducing a lazy KV handoff path plus a configurable degrade schedule that gracefully trades off quality for continuity. This ticket defines the runtime changes, rollout plan, monitoring, and automated fallback behaviors to avoid hard OOMs without large throughput regressions.

Background: Production traces show spikes in KV residency and sudden batch growth at tail traffic causing transient OOMs. Existing measures (aggressive eviction, immediate fallback to smaller models) are either too heavy-handed or cause request failures. We need a middle path that: (1) creates a bounded, async handoff of low-priority KV pages to host spill service, (2) enforces a progressive degrade schedule that reduces per-request memory exposure (token admission reduction, prefix trimming), and (3) triggers hetero-model fallback only as a last resort.

Design summary:
- Lazy KV handoff: inference worker maintains a small lock-free microqueue of KV entries eligible for spill (cold or low-reuse). Instead of synchronous host spill on eviction, eligible entries are enqueued and drained by a dedicated spill thread that rate-limits host I/O based on current GPU headroom. The queue has three priority lanes: hot (never spilled), warm (candidate), cold (immediate enqueue).
- Spill backpressure & admission: if spill queue depth exceeds threshold or spill drain lags, the admission controller starts reducing batch admission window (shorter batch wait) and selectively trims model prefixes for long-context requests. This reduces KV allocation pressure without dropping requests immediately.
- Degrade schedule (progressive): implement a time-and-headroom based state machine with stages: Normal -> Soft Degrade -> Aggressive Degrade -> Model Fallback. Transitions consider metrics: gpu_memory_headroom_pct, kv_occupancy_pct, spill_queue_delay_ms, tail_token_latency_ms, and recent_oom_count. Soft Degrade: 5-15% token admission reduction, enable prefix trimming policy. Aggressive Degrade: 20-50% token drop, enable early-termination heuristics and reduce batch sizes. Model Fallback: route new requests to compatible smaller/quantized model variants (with KV-incompatible requests optionally proxied to host CPU path).
- Retry semantics: requests that are degraded are tagged and optionally retriable by client. Automatic transparent retries within the runtime attempt a small backoff and a second-pass with fallback model if memory pressure persists. Retries must be idempotent for streamed responses; we will add a runtime resume token to allow clients to stitch partial outputs when possible.

Trade-offs considered:
- Latency vs throughput: smaller batches reduce memory but increase per-request latency; the admission controller uses a cost function to bound added latency under SLO.
- Complexity: lazy handoff adds a spill thread and microqueue complexity; chosen because it avoids synchronous host I/O on hot request path.
- Accuracy: progressive degradation keeps a larger fraction of requests served at full fidelity compared to immediate model swap.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Runtime: add spill microqueue and spill-drain thread + prioritization lanes (3 days).
2) Admission controller: hook into batch admission path, expose headroom metrics, implement token-admission throttles and prefix trimmers (4 days).
3) Degrade state machine + policy config: implement tuning knobs and runtime thresholds; wire telemetry (2 days).
4) Fallback routing: extend routing table to map to fallback model variants and add transparent retry/resume token support (3 days).
5) E2E tests and canary harness + chaos tests with synthetic KV storms (4 days).

Observability and metrics to add:
- kv_microqueue_depth_by_lane (int)
- kv_spill_drain_latency_ms_p99
- gpu_memory_headroom_pct (gauge)
- requests_degraded_pct (rolling 1m,5m)
- fallback_model_rate_pct
- degraded_request_latency_p95
- in-flight_retry_rate
- oom_incidents (counter)

Acceptance criteria:
- No hard OOMs in 30-minute synthetic KV storm test at target concurrency (same stress level that previously caused 95th percentile OOMs).
- Requests_degraded_pct stays below configured safety budget (default 15%) during normal traffic.
- Fallover to fallback models reduces oom incidents to zero in heavy load stress tests.
- End-to-end latency SLO (95th) degrades by <= 20% under Soft Degrade compared to baseline.
- Monitoring dashboards and alerts created, and a playbook documented for oncall.

Rollout plan:
- Local dev + unit tests -> staging cluster canary (5% of hosts) with synthetic KV storms -> increase to 25% after 48 hours of stability -> 100% after 7 days if metrics stable. Canary gating includes: oom_incidents==0, degraded_request_latency_p95 within budget, no increase in error rate.

Rollback criteria:
- Any increase in hard OOMs, or sustained degraded_request_latency_p95 > 2x baseline, or increase in customer-facing errors by > 0.5%.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Zero hard OOMs during synthetic KV storm at target concurrency.
2) degraded_request_rate <= safety_budget (default 15%) in normal traffic.
3) fallback model routing reduces OOMs to zero in stress test.
4) telemetry and alerting in place and validated.
